quote: Every time I fill something out where it says get instant code and you fill out information and get no instant code.
stewart_read: Customer voices a specific complaint about repeated unfulfilled contact/lead promises — a legitimacy friction moment.
coaching_implication: Rep should acknowledge the specific frustration by name before pivoting to logistics; a quick 'that sounds frustrating, I want to make sure this visit actually delivers' would rebuild trust faster.

quote: Well, are you gonna be able to install this thing before the texting runs out or not?
stewart_read: Customer reveals urgency tied to the tax credit deadline — a strong forward-pulling hook the rep could have anchored the appointment to.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as skepticism about the timeline rather than enthusiasm, but the phrasing ('before the texting runs out') implies she wants it done, not that she doubts it should happen.
coaching_implication: Rep confirmed feasibility generically ('We should be able to') instead of using her urgency to lock the appointment emotionally to the deadline.

quote: Is there anyone else on the title with you?
stewart_read: Co-owner captured by name only; rep never asked about his general availability at this point in the call, only much later after booking was underway.
coaching_implication: Ask co-owner availability immediately after capturing the name, not after a time slot is already being negotiated.

stewart_read: Rep asks once when the co-owner would be available, gets 'Never,' and proceeds to book the customer alone without further resolution.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep gave up after one attempt. Strategic read would require evidence rep planned to loop him in separately, but none exists.
coaching_implication: Per protocols.spouse_decision, co-decider must be included; rep should have asked for any window (even a quick call-in) rather than dropping it after one no.

quote: how much on average are you paying a month?
stewart_read: Bill amount captured cleanly but rep moves immediately to the next qualifier with no acknowledgment or emotional flip.
coaching_implication: A quick reflection ('and that's before rates keep climbing') would set up the inversion move later; instead it's filed silently.

quote: is just your most current utility bill that just shows us exactly how much energy you're using for the home. Do you get those through the mail or online?
stewart_read: Bill collection runs mechanically with no curiosity-building language about what the design will show her; large silent gap (03:41 to 04:42) suggests dead air while she retrieves the bill.
coaching_implication: Rep could bridge the wait with a forward-looking tease about what the design review will cover, instead of just holding the line silently.
